# Status

What works, what is partial, and where the open work is. The headline is
rendered from the gates, never typed:

```
scripts/gates.sh > gates.log 2>&1    # every gate; red on any regression
cargo xtask status-md                # the headline below, from that run
```

If a number anywhere disagrees with those commands, the commands are right.
The open work, partitioned and ordered, is
[`plans/sprint-parity.md`](plans/sprint-parity.md); what each gate
grades is in [`architecture.md`](architecture.md#the-gates).

The table is rendered from the last green `scripts/gates.sh` run
(`target/gates/status.json`) by `cargo xtask status-md`, which refuses a red
run or one made from another tree. How each number moved is in `git log`
and [`journal.md`](journal.md); the per-item sets behind every ratcheted row
are in `baseline.json`.

`conformance` asks "is every assertion the frontend should decide decided
correctly?" Since 2026-10-10 the frontend is graded as complete
(`FRONTEND_COMPLETE`, the owner's decision): an `expected:1` snippet that
compiles cleanly, or a warning not raised, is a failure, so `conformance`
and `--strict` grade the same. What stays undecidable is the 241 assertions
that expect a specific C++ backend code; the frontend must *not* diagnose
those earlier than the reference ([`known-divergences.md`](known-divergences.md)),
and `backend` grades them end to end.

## What the compiler is today (2026-10-10)

```
source ─ kg-parser/kg-syntax ─▶ CST ─ kg-resolve ─▶ names, module graph
   │                              │
   │                              └─ kg-db, per module at its text (CST): the parser's
   │                                 own checks and pass 1; every later pass the loop's
   ▼
kg-hir: the sorted lowering ─▶ IR per module
   │
   ▼
kg-sem::elaborate — the program-wide loop, passes 2–8 on the IR:
   higherOrderFunctions, captureThis, deduceTemplateArgs, intrinsics,
   inferType (incremental), trimExternClasses, then rounds of
   addLambdaWrappers · desugarLambdas · abbreviatedFunctionTemplate ·
   moveFunctions · closureCalls · deduce · census · instantiate,
   deduplicateInstances at the end
   │
   ├─ kg-sem::check — the passes after instantiation, over the copies,
   │    and at each module's text for 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14 and
   │    16–19 (sprint W3 step 1)
   ├─ kg-db::looped — the loop's trees, types and parse, as the parser's
   │    checks and the editor read them — the one engine (sprint W3.7)
   ▼
kg-ptbridge — the walk into the ParseTree C ABI, replayed in a worker
into the reference's C++ backend (libkanagawa-backend) ─▶ RTL
```

`kg check` runs everything above the walk; `kg build` and the compat
`kanagawa` binary run all of it. Against the reference's own frontend,
`kg check` is 5–9× faster ([`plans/performance.md`](plans/performance.md)
§11).

## Frontend passes

Execution order ([`spec/frontend-passes.md`](spec/frontend-passes.md)): the
reference's `desugarPasses` fold with `foldr ($)`, so the *last* entry runs
first. `hasErrors` checkpoints after passes 1, 8 and 9 decide which errors a
rejected program shows (`Frontend.hs:38-52`), reproduced per file — and,
for a verdict that something was left undecided (passes 16 and 17, since
2026-10-10), program-wide as well: another module's error can be its whole
reason (`Db::program_erred_through_pass_9`). The loop's verdicts enter a
module's run at their own pass — at its text in the moved pass's place, in
its copies at the pass each is the reference's (`kg_sem::check::Stage`) —
so none closes a checkpoint before it (2026-10-10).

"CST" is `kg-db`'s per-module pass over the concrete tree, reading the
loop's types and what the parser built (`kg_db::parsed`) — no type table
of its own since the CST inference engine was deleted (sprint W3.7); "IR"
is `kg-sem`'s over the program's IR; "copies" is `kg_sem::check`, which
reports inside instantiated copies at the template body with `while
compiling` frames.

Loading-time diagnostics — a failed or circular import, a namespace that
disagrees with its path, `checkExposed`, the `redundant-import` warning —
are `kg_db`'s (`Program::diagnostics`), not passes.

## The tools

| Front door | State |
|---|---|
| `kg check` | the frontend, every diagnostic above, rendered with source excerpts; the C++ backend's own verdicts are `kg build`'s |
| `kg build`, `kanagawa` (compat) | compile to RTL through the reference's backend, run in a worker process. `kanagawa` takes the reference's every mode and flag — `compile`, `list-deps`, `--file-list`, `--template-iterations`, `--help` byte for byte (`xtask cli` 25/25, upstream's own CLI tests among them) and its diagnostics laid out as the reference's; `pretty` and the `--dump-*` trees are refused by decision (`known-divergences.md` #34–#38) |
| `kg fmt` | comment-preserving formatter; `fmt-check` proves 405/405 files idempotent and structurally unchanged |
| `kg lsp` | diagnostics, quick fixes (a diagnostic's fix, the cast `TypeCheck.hs:103` hints, since 2026-10-10), goto-definition (an import's path to its module's file since 2026-10-10), go to type definition (the loop's type's declaration, since 2026-10-10), hover, references and rename (the project's files, each under its own program, since 2026-10-10), completion, signature help, inlay hints, symbols (the file's outline, and every open program's by name since 2026-10-10), folding, selection ranges, highlight, semantic tokens; keystroke worst case 1.46 s (sprint W7: ≤ 400 ms, then ≤ 100 ms with M6); diagnostics read the loop — at four rounds first, then from the same run at its fixpoint, `kg check`'s (2026-10-10, sprint W7.6; the other features read the newest of the two ready); hover, inlay hints, signature help, completion and go-to-definition on a field read it too wherever the diagnostics run it — inside a template's body, every instance's type; a member list or a `.f` jump through the loop's type of the base, an instance's copy included (`a.` on a `Box<4>` lists `items` `uint32[4]`) — completion once the diagnostics have computed it, never waiting; methods too (2026-10-10): go-to-definition on `c.go()`, an instance's method, a member template (`fixture.Run<3>(t)`) lands on the class's text, and a member the instances declare apart (a `static if`) offers each; hover shows the member as the receiver's instance has it, a member template's call the instance it compiles; references, rename and highlight find uses through receivers the loop types — in a file nobody has open, through a loop of its own — and a rename refuses where a `.f` cannot be placed or the search stopped at its bound; on a buffer that does not parse (2026-10-10, sprint W3.4) every one of these reads the last loop computed for the program, mapped through the edit by a line diff — `a.` typed in a template instance's method lists that instance's members — and a buffer opened broken runs its own loop once, for a hover. The loop is the one engine (sprint W3.7): text no loop has seen, a declaration in a redefinition (which no program holds), and — until a loop runs — a buffer opened broken show no type, list no members and get no hint, where the deleted CST engine answered |
| `kg dump`, `kg explain` | tokens / CST / AST / IR / the instances the loop made (by template, each as a `while compiling` note spells it, with its round and site; sprint W3.7); error and warning explanations |
